benefit.name: Fair PharmaCare
benefit.amount: Income-based drug coverage. Family net income of $13,750 or less: PharmaCare pays 100 percent of eligible costs from the first prescription. Up to $30,000: no deductible, with a family maximum between $100 and $800. Above that a deductible applies, then PharmaCare pays 70 percent, and 100 percent once you reach your family maximum.
benefit.summary: BC's main drug plan for anyone enrolled in MSP. It pays a share of your eligible prescriptions based on family net income. The lower your income, the sooner and the more it pays. Free to register.

benefit.requiresNote: Any MSP-enrolled BC resident or family can register. Your assistance level is scaled to family net income from two years earlier, verified with the CRA.
benefit.note: Return the consent form within 30 days of registering. If you do not, temporary coverage ends and your family's deductible is set at $10,000. Also, if you are moving into a long-term care facility, ask whether it is enrolled in PharmaCare Plan B before you move in. Plan B gives permanent residents of enrolled facilities 100% coverage of eligible prescription drugs and pharmacy services. It also covers eligible medical supplies up to a maximum. It is automatic, with no application. But not all facilities are enrolled. It does not apply to assisted-living, extended-care, acute-care or temporary respite or hospice stays.

detail.about: Assistance is tied to family net income from two years prior and coverage applies automatically at the pharmacy counter. After a family meets its deductible PharmaCare pays 70% of eligible costs, or 75% if a family member was born before 1940. After a family reaches its family maximum, Fair PharmaCare pays 100% of eligible costs for the rest of the year.

steps: Gather the Personal Health Number for every family member, Social Insurance Numbers for adults, and the adults' tax information from two years ago
Register online, or call Health Insurance BC if online registration is not accessible to you
Use the temporary coverage that begins the same day while income verification is pending
Sign and return the CRA consent form within 30 days so temporary coverage does not end
Check your registration status online or call if a pharmacy cannot see the coverage

The CRA consent deadline matters: return it within 30 days
If family income has dropped substantially, ask PharmaCare whether an income review is available

If you or a family member is moving into long-term care, ask whether the facility is registered with PharmaCare Plan B before moving in. Plan B covers 100% of eligible prescription drugs and pharmacy services for permanent residents of registered facilities. It also covers eligible medical supplies up to a maximum price set by PharmaCare. It starts automatically. But not every facility is registered.

Plan B does not apply to extended-care, acute-care, multi-level or assisted-living facilities. It also does not apply to a short-term stay in a long-term care facility, such as a temporary stay for respite care, hospice or palliative care.

Since March 1, 2026, PharmaCare's National Pharmacare plan, Plan NP, has covered many diabetes medications, contraceptives and menopausal hormone therapy at no cost to you. Coverage is automatic at the pharmacy. There is nothing to register for and no receipts to submit. You must be a B.C. resident enrolled in MSP, and the prescription must be dispensed in B.C.
Plan NP prescriptions do not count towards your Fair PharmaCare deductible or family maximum. So they cost you nothing, but they also do not move you closer to meeting your deductible.

The Plan NP diabetes list includes insulins, metformin, glyburide, gliclazide, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin, and combinations of them. A few others need Special Authority approval before a pharmacy can fill them. These include saxagliptin, linagliptin and pioglitazone. Ask your prescriber.
On April 1, 2026, Plan NP expanded to cover certain diabetes-related supplies and devices.

PharmaCare also covers the full cost of nicotine gum, lozenges and patches for one continuous course of up to 12 weeks (84 days) in a calendar year. The allowance resets on January 1. You and the pharmacist both sign a declaration form at the pharmacy, so there is nothing to apply for in advance. You must be enrolled in MSP, but you do not need to be signed up for Fair PharmaCare. Certain prescription stop-smoking drugs are covered instead through Fair PharmaCare or through Plans B, C, G or W.
